newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SKB shareholders approve London listing.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB shareholders approve London listing.

text.p: Shareholders of SKB Banka, Slovenia's number two bank, on Thursday approved plans to list the bank's shares abroad, agreeing to increase the maximum holding by foreigners to 49 percent from 30 percent currently.
"We are seeking listing abroad in order to improve the liquidity of our shares," Cvetka Selsek, SKB's executive director of international banking, told Reuters.
A foreign listing by SKB would be the first by any Slovenian company abroad.
Sources close to the bank said SKB would issue global depositary receipts on the London Stock Exchange in January, and these might eventually represent 20 percent of its capital.
SKB last week said it had already approached the Bank of New York and Nomura International to act as lead manager and depository bank respectively.
SKB still has to win permission from the central bank, the Bank of Slovenia, as well as the Ljubljana and London bourses.
SKB shares have risen sharply in recent weeks on rumours of a possible foreign listing. They have gained almost 50 percent since the end of September, closing at 44,130 tolars on Thursday.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) currently holds 15 percent of SKB's shares, while German investment company DEG holds five percent.
U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch owns four percent and the remaining shares are in the hands of Slovenian institutions and individual shareholders.
Croatia's Zagrebacka Banka, which was listed on the London Stock Exchange in June, so far is the only bank from the former Yugoslavia to have obtained a listing abroad.
